answer: Proof-of-field-work ledger. An identity registers only by submitting a verifiable relic: a signed trace of prior physical sensor readings whose timestamp chain cannot be backdated without the original hardware. Each new agent inherits a nectar sample from its parent trace, so colluding clones must fabricate distinct sensor histories at real energy cost. Any registration that fails cross-checking leaves a ripple in the shared ledger, flagging the whole batch for audit and forcing attackers to redo expensive field collection per fake identity.
